title: Notice of Charges — Late Payment on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans
content:
# Notice of Charges — Late Payment on Belrose Promotional Financing Plans

A scheduled payment on a Belrose Promotional Financing Plan not settled by its due date carries a late fee once the term's grace period has run out. The grace period, the first-lateness and repeat fees, the repeat window, the fee ceiling and the automatic payment grace are the figures the fee schedule states for the plan's promotional term.

## When a payment becomes late

A late fee is charged only when the handling date has passed the payment due date printed on the statement for that billing cycle extended by the grace period of the term, and equality with that boundary does not yet make the payment late. Grace is counted in whole calendar days from the payment due date, never in twenty-four hour periods, the day of the due date itself counting as day zero, and where the resulting boundary falls on a day the business does not open the boundary still stands on that calendar day. The due date is the one printed on the statement entry in the plan's billing history; the customer's recollection of the due date is not the basis.

### The boundary, on hypothetical dates

Suppose a statement prints a payment due date of the 10th of a month and the term's grace period is 3 days. The boundary day is the 13th.

| Handling date | Late? |
|---|---|
| The 12th | No: the boundary has not been reached |
| The 13th (the boundary day itself) | No: equality with the boundary does not yet make the payment late |
| The 14th | Yes: the handling date has passed the boundary |

The boundary stands on the 13th even where the 13th is a day the business does not open.

## While the plan stands

A late fee is charged only while the plan stands at active or past due, as the plan record shows.

## Which fee, and how much

The clause that read "The first lateness inside the term's repeat window carries the first-lateness fee and a later one inside the same window carries the repeat fee, the window being the rolling number of whole months the term sets and counted backwards from the missed due date." is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for the lateness charge. The term's first-lateness fee, repeat fee and repeat window remain the figures the fee schedule states.

No single late fee exceeds the term's ceiling expressed as a share of the scheduled monthly payment, and where a plan is delinquent for several cycles one fee arises per missed due date and never more than one.

## Automatic payment that failed through no fault of the customer

Where automatic payment failed through no fault of the customer the fee is not charged at all for a replacement payment made inside the term's automatic payment grace, and that non-charge is not a courtesy give-back: it consumes no courtesy allowance and is not recorded as a give-back.
